listing.description:
Paseo on Fifth is a vibrant new residential development in the heart of Park Slope, Brooklyn. Nestled within The Paseo—a thoughtfully designed pedestrian passage where Fifth Avenue meets Sterling Place—this one-of-a-kind address offers a peaceful retreat amid the energy of the neighborhood. Framed by curated retail and local charm, The Paseo fosters a unique sense of community and calm just steps from home.

Enter the exquisite residences at Paseo on Fifth, where sophisticated design meets modern practicality. From airy studios to expansive two-bedroom apartments, explore a range of layouts with luxurious finishes to enhance your daily living. Residences feature up to 10’ 9” ceiling heights, wide plank flooring in a light oak finish, and floor-to-ceiling windows that flood interiors with natural light. Quartz countertops, custom tile work, and Kohler fixtures with rainfall showerheads elevate kitchens and baths with refined detail, while stainless steel appliances from Bosch and Samsung add modern functionality.

At Paseo on Fifth, you will find an amenities suite that truly harmonizes with your daily rhythm. Dive into a meticulously designed environment where everything from the cutting-edge gym and yoga studio to the plush coworking spaces transforms everyday tasks into elements of a curated lifestyle. Seamlessly transition from productivity in our high-tech workspaces to relaxation in The Hub, each space crafted with a keen eye for function and style.

• Virtual Doorman
• Rooftop Garden
• Lobby Lounge
• Coworking Lounge
• The Library
• Second Floor Terrace
• Crafts Studio
• Smart Package Room
• Bike Storage
• Laundry Convenience
• Storage
• Valet Parking

*Tenant Fees & Responsibilities*
Prospective residents are responsible for the following fees, subject to lease or service agreement terms:
Application Fee: $20 per person
Security Deposit: 1 month’s rent
Amenities Fee: $50/month per tenant
Storage: $50 - $75/month
Bike Storage: $15/Month per bike
Pet Fee: $25/month per pet
Utilities: Rent includes hot water and sewage; residents cover electricity, cable, and internet.

Marketed by Compass Development Marketing Group.

listing.description:
Paseo on Fifth is a vibrant new residential development in the heart of Park Slope, Brooklyn. Nestled within The Paseo—a thoughtfully designed pedestrian passage where Fifth Avenue meets Sterling Place—this one-of-a-kind address offers a peaceful retreat amid the energy of the neighborhood. Framed by curated retail and local charm, The Paseo fosters a unique sense of community and calm just steps from home.

Enter the exquisite residences at Paseo on Fifth, where sophisticated design meets modern practicality. From airy studios to expansive two-bedroom apartments, explore a range of layouts with luxurious finishes to enhance your daily living. Residences feature up to 10’ 9” ceiling heights, wide plank flooring in a light oak finish, and floor-to-ceiling windows that flood interiors with natural light. Quartz countertops, custom tile work, and Kohler fixtures with rainfall showerheads elevate kitchens and baths with refined detail, while stainless steel appliances from Bosch and Samsung add modern functionality.

At Paseo on Fifth, you will find an amenities suite that truly harmonizes with your daily rhythm. Dive into a meticulously designed environment where everything from the cutting-edge gym and yoga studio to the plush coworking spaces transforms everyday tasks into elements of a curated lifestyle. Seamlessly transition from productivity in our high-tech workspaces to relaxation in The Hub, each space crafted with a keen eye for function and style.

listing.description:
FORT GREENE — RARE FULLY DETACHED PRIVATE RESIDENCE!

A truly exceptional rental opportunity in the heart of vibrant Fort Greene. This completely detached, beautifully restored townhouse offers the privacy, space, and outdoor living rarely found in Brooklyn—complete with a secured gated entrance, private front and rear yards, and video intercom access.

This stunning, fully renovated duplex features oversized windows, abundant natural light, multi-zone central heating and air conditioning, generous storage, and high-end finishes throughout.

The spacious, airy living and dining area flows seamlessly into a chef’s kitchen featuring extensive cabinetry, a full pantry, quartz countertops, new dishwasher, and a large center island with bar seating—perfect for everyday living and entertaining.

Upstairs, the exceptionally large primary bedroom includes three double closets, a private en-suite bathroom, and ample space for a dedicated home office or sitting area. An in-unit brand new washer and dryer are conveniently located in a separate laundry area.

Tenants are responsible for all utilities. No smoking. Pets considered on a case-by-case basis. Available September 15.

Sales Median asking price 1 bed $899K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,650 Bisected by Flatbush Avenue and bordered by the BQE, Downtown Brooklyn is a rapidly expanding residential neighborhood. Easy subway access and abundant inventory have drawn many to the area looking for luxury rentals and condos in the area's numerous new apartment towers. Historically, Downtown Brooklyn has been the hub of the borough's municipal activities with many civil service offices and court houses centered around Cadman Plaza, the neighborhood's main hub. With tons of city employees, lawyers and Brooklynites of all types constantly bustling about, Downtown Brooklyn has a decidedly hectic vibe. This, coupled with the area's lack of green space, makes Downtown Brooklyn most appealing to those who can embrace one of Brooklyn's busiest and most trafficked neighborhoods. Sales Median asking price 1 bed $950K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $4,325 Energetic and inviting, Boerum Hill continues its run as one of New York City's most desirable neighborhoods, all while remaining a secret quietly shared amongst its happy residents. Its appeal and vibrancy stem from its housing stock. Handsome Greek revival and Italianate townhouses line the wide, tree-lined streets. These beautiful brick and limestone buildings have long been a mecca for Brooklynites seeking an enclave close to Downtown Brooklyn and lower Manhattan — but far from crowds and highrises. Main drags like Bergen Street, Atlantic Avenue, and Smith Street are peppered with charming boutiques like Collier West in addition to welcoming cafes, bars, and restaurants, including Rucola, French Louie, and Bacchus, to name a few. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block. listing.description:
Park block! Bright and beautifully renovated, this two-bedroom apartment offers the convenience of an in-unit washer and dryer with high-end, front-loading LG machines. Located on the first floor, the apartment is easily accessible while sitting comfortably above street level thanks to the building’s stoop.

The open kitchen is thoughtfully equipped with a dishwasher, five-burner gas range, built-in microwave, and generous cabinet and counter space. Both bedrooms comfortably accommodate queen-size beds and are nicely separated by a hallway with a convenient coat closet. The stylishly tiled bathroom also includes a linen closet.

Ideally situated in prime Park Slope, just one block from Prospect Park and three short blocks from the F and G trains, with an abundance of restaurants, cafés, and shopping nearby.

Available in September. No pets, please. Guarantors accepted.

*Photos are of this unit. Video is of the unit next door that is a mirror image of #4 with the same finishes and layout.

Sales Median asking price 1 bed $699K Rentals Median asking base rent 1 bed $3,895 When George Washington commandeered the building site that would eventually become Gracie Mansion, he probably didn't imagine that this peaceful, riverside enclave would become the lively residential neighborhood it is today. Between then and now, Yorkville has seen a lot of change. Tony mansions and elevated trains went up at the turn of the century and then came down in the postwar years as a middle-class population moved in. Now, the neighborhood is a haven of high-rise co-ops and condos interspersed with quiet rows of townhouses. The mixed housing stock makes Yorkville a practical choice for anyone seeking a slowed-down Manhattan vibe. Several avenues over from the throngs of Lexington and Third Avenues, Yorkville maintains a low-key, no-frills feel — it's a place where you'll find more diners and donut shops than upscale lounges and boutiques. This homey attitude is writ in its storefronts, where the food is kept simple and the owners are often from around the block.
